doc.title: Red Holloway interviewed by Monk Rowe and Michael Woods, Scottsdale, Arizona, March 4, 1995

title: First road job with Roosevelt Sykes in 1948
summary: His mother knew Roosevelt Sykes, and his first road gig was a year touring the country with Sykes, which taught him the blues. He also contrasts his classical conservatory training with today's jazz studies.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: Yeah, and so the thing is, it’s something that you have to feel. And I was around more blues players. In fact, my mother and Roosevelt Sykes went to school together. And my first gig on the road was with Roosevelt Sykes for a year, 1948. I went all over the U.S.
with him. So now when you’re playing the blues every night, you got to, you can’t help but know the blues, and feel the blues. So that was one of the, that’s really how I got started, and that’s—
That’s still part of your playing today.
Oh, yeah. I still love the blues.
